QuakeScope 2026 — western catalogue

Machine-learning P and S picks for the western United States and its neighbours, 1986 to September 2026: Washington, Oregon, California, Nevada, Idaho and Wyoming, plus Utah, Montana, Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, British Columbia, Alberta, Baja California and Sonora.

What happened to every station-day

From western/availability/, one row per station-day inside a station's operating epochs (54,355,276 rows). Statuses before image d0ccf9b are coarser: those shards recorded only what they read, which is why unknown exists.

statusmeaningstation-days
loadedread and picked16,965,900

unknowninside the station's epochs, no record either way24,621,886

Do the manifests match the data?

The Parquet holds duplicate picks. 12,125 objects (69,690,152 picks) are listed by no manifest: files written by shard attempts that Spot interrupted before the shard was re-run. In a random sample of 200 of them, 92.2% of rows also appear in a listed file (101 objects fully duplicated, 83 partly, 16 not at all). Estimated unique picks: ~2.066 billion of 2,130,446,013 rows (about 64.3 million duplicates). Until they are removed, de-duplicate on (tid, cha, pha, peak) when reading.

How it was made

PhaseNet, original weights (SeisBench 0.12.5, weight version 2), P and S thresholds 0.2, components ZNE12. Picks are written per shard as Parquet partitioned by network, year and month; each shard writes a manifest; since image d0ccf9b every planned station-day also gets an outcome. The catalogue was built by these queues, all writing into the same prefix:

Gaps

Networks our EarthScope account may not read (TD, EO, LH); NP strong-motion (no data in a 1,408-day sample, not re-read); 673,676 station-days in scattered short gaps; 328 station-days whose day files crash the miniSEED decoder (SF.PH004-006 2006-07, X7.LB01 2008) and 678 whose day object exceeds 4 GB.

Cost

Estimated, not billed: compute hours priced at $0.0213 per vCPU-hour, a rate calibrated on CloudBank's billed costs for three days of full load. The account cannot read AWS cost APIs. Storage of this catalogue is about $1.27 a month in S3 Standard; public downloads cost about $0.09 per GB once the account's free tier is used.

Reading it

Public, anonymous, no account: reading tutorial · region and period · data access guide. Cite the prefix and the date you read it.
